note: Défendre means defend/protect but also forbid/prohibit in the construction défendre de. That common learner meaning is missing.
proposed_english: to defend; to protect; to forbid/prohibit (défendre de)

note: Avance is a noun meaning advance/progress (and advance payment) and also a common finite/imperative form of avancer. The current POS is noun-only despite mentioning a verb form.
proposed_english: advance; progress; advance payment; advances/moves forward; advance!/move forward! (forms of avancer, context-dependent)
proposed_pos: noun / finite verb form / imperative form

note: Sexe is a noun meaning sex, gender/biological sex, and sex/genitals depending on context. 'Sexy' and 'pornographic' are not meanings of the noun sexe and are misleading dictionary noise.
proposed_english: sex; biological sex; gender (context-dependent); genitals/sex organs (context-dependent)

note: Arbre centrally means tree. The current entry omits 'tree' entirely and lists only mechanical shaft/axle senses.

Soit is not only a conjunction: it is also the present subjunctive form of être and can function as an acceptance/discourse expression ('so be it/okay') or in explanatory use ('namely'). POS must reflect the listed meanings.
proposed_english: either; whether; be (present subjunctive of être); namely/that is; okay/so be it
proposed_pos: conjunction / verb form / adverbial or discourse expression

note: Criminel means criminal as an adjective or noun. 'Crime' is not the English meaning of criminel and should be removed.
Traîner means drag/pull but also the very common intransitive hang around/linger/loiter and be delayed/drag on. The current entry is too narrow.
proposed_english: to drag; to pull; to hang around; to linger/loiter; to drag on

note: Secours means help/aid/rescue/assistance; first aid is only one compound use (premiers secours). The one-gloss entry is too narrow.
proposed_english: help; aid; assistance; rescue; first aid (premiers secours)

note: Politique is both the noun policy/politics and the adjective political. Adjective POS is listed but its meaning is omitted.
Été is the noun summer and also the extremely common past participle of être, meaning been in compound constructions. Omitting that homograph is a major learner defect.
Programme is a noun and also a common finite/imperative form of programmer. For a form-based frequency workbook, that homograph should be explicit.
proposed_english: program/programme; schedule; plan; programs/schedules; program!/schedule! (forms of programmer, context-dependent)
proposed_pos: noun / finite verb form / imperative form

note: Baisser means lower, decrease, go down/fall, or lower/bend something. 'To fail' is not an appropriate core gloss and should be removed.
proposed_english: to lower; to decrease; to go down; to fall; to lower/bend
